summary.tagline: Wander through ancient woodlands and open heathlands where free-roaming livestock shape the landscape.
summary.seo_title: New Forest National Park Trip Guide: Nature & Trails

travel.headline: Follow the New Forest Code for a Responsible Visit
travel.reservation: While there is no general park entry permit, you must follow the New Forest Code to protect rare ground-nesting birds and free-roaming livestock. Camping is only permitted at designated sites and no fires or BBQs are allowed anywhere in the forest; check with local landowners for specific permissions regarding activities like metal detecting.

days.title: Ancient Trees and Accessible Trails

stops.name: Blackwater Arboretum
stops.detail: Explore a unique collection of trees from around the world on a short, accessible trail.

stops.name: Brockenhurst Village
stops.detail: Visit this charming village to experience the local pace and see free-roaming animals grazing near the roadside.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers; livestock may cause delays.
days.note: Keep your distance from ponies and donkeys at all times.

days.title: Lakeside Wildlife and Forest Vistas

stops.name: Blashford Lakes
stops.detail: A peaceful area featuring accessible trails ideal for spotting local birds and nature.

stops.name: Burley Village
stops.detail: Walk through this famous forest village known for its local character and easy 4-mile circular trail.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; conditions vary by weather and animal activity.
days.note: Keep to the main tracks to avoid disturbing rare ground-nesting birds.

days.title: Village Strolls and Coastal Edge

stops.name: Ashurst Stroll
stops.detail: An easy 2.5-mile walk that provides a gentle introduction to the forest landscape.

stops.name: Boldre Village

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; use the New Forest Tour open-top bus for sustainable travel.
days.note: Stick to waymarked tracks especially during breeding season from February to August.

intel.title: Track Access
intel.text: Keep to main tracks to protect rare ground-nesting birds, particularly between February and August. Walking off-track is discouraged in sensitive habitats.

intel.title: Designated Parking
intel.text: The New Forest Code requires parking only in official car parks to protect the verges. Avoid parking on grass or blocking gateways.

intel.title: Pony Safety
intel.text: Drive with care as animals have right of way on all forest roads. Night driving requires extra caution due to low visibility of free-roaming livestock.

intel.title: Connectivity
intel.text: Signal varies significantly across the open heath and deep woods. Download the New Forest National Park Walks app before entering remote areas.

intel.title: Local Supplies
intel.text: Support the local economy by looking for the New Forest Marque emblem in village stores. Most major services are found in gateway towns like Ringwood or Southampton.

plan.arrival: Arrive via train to Brockenhurst or Ashurst for sustainable access. Pick up local supplies in village centers and look for the New Forest Marque accreditation on regional products.
plan.vehicle: Cars are suitable but drivers must observe the special forest speed limits to protect animals; the open-top New Forest Tour bus is a sustainable seasonal alternative.
plan.goldenHour: Deer Watch Trail during late afternoon for the best chance to spot wildlife from a respectful distance.
